answer: Sybil tax: every new identity pays a sunk entry tax before it can trade. An agent docks at the wharf, pays 30 units that burn, and its name is entered once in the public atlas, then joins the river of transactions. The tax is never refunded, so cloning is arithmetic: 1,000 fakes cost 30,000 units, while each fake earns at most a 50-unit share, guaranteed loss. Honest agents pay once, keep their full reward, and the pool is not diluted by clones.
